Title: Mapping spatial distribution and biomass of coastal wetland vegetation in Indonesian Papua by combining active and passive remotely sensed data
Key Findings: Combined SAR and multispectral imagery effectively maps mangrove biomass. Highlighted benefits of multi-sensor fusion in cloudy equatorial regions.

Title: The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation: High-resolution laser ranging of the Earth's forests and topography
Key Findings: Introduced NASA GEDI as gold standard for canopy height. Noted sparse coverage outside equatorial orbital paths.

Title: Mangrove canopy height globally related to precipitation, temperature and cyclone frequency
Key Findings: Global mangrove height mapping using SRTM. Showed environmental drivers of canopy height.

Title: Estimating and mapping above-ground biomass of mangrove species using Sentinel-2 and machine learning
Key Findings: Machine learning (Random Forest) effectively maps AGB from Sentinel-2, but lacks 3D structural data for high accuracy.

Title: Landscape-scale extent, height, biomass, and carbon estimation of Mozambique's eco-region
Key Findings: Early use of SRTM and Landsat for mangrove AGB. Established need for active 3D sensors.

Title: Aboveground biomass estimation using GEDI in tropical forests
Key Findings: Validated GEDI AGB algorithms. Showed high accuracy in dense forests but missing data issues in arid/subtropical fringes.

Title: Integrating Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 for mangrove mapping in arid coastal zones
Key Findings: Arid mangroves (like UAE) have different spectral signatures from tropical ones. Radar VV/VH ratio helps distinguish canopy from wet sand.

Title: Large-scale mangrove AGB estimation combining GEDI and optical data
Source: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation
Key Findings: Fusing GEDI and Sentinel-2 improves AGB estimation, but performance drops where GEDI footprints are sparse.

Title: Assessment of Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data for mangrove forest classification
Key Findings: Cloud-penetrating SAR (S1) paired with optical (S2) drastically improves classification accuracy in coastal zones.

Title: Domain adaptation for the classification of remote sensing data: An overview of recent advances
Source: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine
Key Findings: Domain adaptation allows models trained in data-rich areas to apply to data-poor areas.

Title: Global canopy height regression and uncertainty estimation from GEDI and Sentinel-2 using neural networks
Key Findings: Neural networks can impute global canopy height continuously by learning the relationship between GEDI (sparse) and Sentinel-2 (dense).

Title: Deep learning classification of land cover and crop types using remote sensing data
Source: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
Key Findings: Deep learning outperforms RF for remote sensing, but requires large contiguous datasets.

Title: A generalizable and accessible approach to machine learning with global satellite imagery
Key Findings: Transfer learning enables robust spatial prediction models across different biomes.

Title: Missing data imputation in remote sensing: A review of deep learning methods
Key Findings: Autoencoders and CNNs are highly effective at imputing missing satellite gaps caused by clouds or orbital paths.

Title: Transfer learning for mangrove above-ground biomass estimation across regions
Key Findings: Models trained on Asian mangroves can be transferred to African mangroves, but require local fine-tuning.

Title: Deep learning in remote sensing: A comprehensive review and list of resources
Source: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine
Key Findings: Highlights the necessity of multimodal data fusion (Radar+Optical+LiDAR) using ANNs.

Title: Semi-supervised classification with graph convolutional networks
Key Findings: Introduced standard GCNs. Demonstrated how spatial topology can be leveraged for feature aggregation.

Title: Spatio-temporal graph convolutional networks: A deep learning framework for traffic forecasting
Key Findings: Pioneered ST-GNN architectures, capturing both spatial topology and temporal dynamics simultaneously.

Title: Connecting the dots: Multivariate time series forecasting with graph neural networks
Key Findings: GNNs are superior for forecasting when individual nodes have hidden relational dependencies.

Title: River network modeling using Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks
Key Findings: Applied ST-GNN to hydrological flows, showing that directional edges map perfectly to natural water networks.

Title: Predicting forest fire spread using graph neural networks
Key Findings: Graph nodes representing forest patches allow better prediction of environmental spread dynamics than pixel-based CNNs.

Title: Ecosystem carbon flux modeling using spatial graphs
Key Findings: Spatial graphs improve carbon flux estimation compared to isolated point-based models, but lacked temporal sequence modelling.

Title: Spatio-temporal graph modeling for environmental monitoring
Key Findings: ST-GNNs are highly robust against missing data in environmental sensor networks.

Title: Blue carbon as a natural climate solution
Key Findings: Mangroves are powerful carbon sinks, but MRV costs and verification uncertainties block market scaling.

Title: Global carbon stocks and potential emissions due to mangrove deforestation
Key Findings: Highlights the massive carbon density of mangroves and the need for standardized global tracking.

Title: High-resolution carbon monitoring systems for forest ecosystems
Key Findings: Manual MRV is too slow; automated satellite-based MRV is the only path to national-scale carbon accounting.

Title: VM0033 Methodology for Tidal Wetland and Seagrass Restoration
Key Findings: Strict guidelines on autochthonous vs allochthonous carbon, Additionality, and Permanence.

Title: The role of digital technologies in carbon markets
Key Findings: Digital MRV reduces carbon project certification costs by up to 70% but faces regulatory skepticism.

Title: The potential of Indonesian mangrove forests for global climate change mitigation
Key Findings: Establishes baselines for mangrove soil carbon density, forming the basis of many blue carbon credit calculations.

Title: Global patterns in mangrove soil carbon stocks and losses
Key Findings: Soil carbon is highly dependent on tidal flushing and geomorphology, proving pixels cannot be treated independently.

Title: UAE National Blue Carbon Programme: COP28 Progress Report
Key Findings: Outlines the UAE's 100 million mangrove goal and the critical need for scalable local verification mechanisms.

Title: Supplement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories: Wetlands
Key Findings: Classifies mangrove carbon as Blue Carbon under international climate frameworks.

Title: Allometry, biomass, and productivity of mangrove forests: A review
Key Findings: Established foundational allometric equations for mangrove biomass estimation used as baseline worldwide.

Title: A unified approach to interpreting model predictions
Key Findings: Introduced SHAP based on game theory to explain individual machine learning predictions reliably.

Title: Interpretable Machine Learning
Key Findings: Defines the need for feature attribution in high-stakes domains where black-box models are unacceptable.

Title: Explainable Machine Learning for Scientific Insights and Discoveries
Key Findings: XAI transforms ML from a predictive tool to a scientific discovery tool by highlighting feature interactions.

Title: Predicting supply chain risks using machine learning: The trade-off between performance and interpretability
Key Findings: Auditors require interpretability. Models without SHAP/LIME fail regulatory compliance checks.

Title: Using SHAP to interpret deep learning models in environmental monitoring
Key Findings: SHAP effectively identifies specific weather variables (e.g. temperature spikes) driving environmental anomalies.

Title: Auditable AI: The role of explainability in climate-tech
Method: Policy Analysis of XAI in Carbon Markets
Key Findings: Carbon markets require 'Auditable AI', which necessitates SHAP or similar methods to prove Additionality.

Title: Fooling LIME and SHAP: Adversarial Attacks on Post hoc Explanation Methods
Key Findings: Warns of vulnerabilities in XAI, establishing the need for cross-referencing SHAP outputs with external evidence (like news/weather).
